original_value: AbstractThe Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe), a founding member of the Worldwide Protein Data Bank (wwPDB), actively participates in the deposition, curation, validation, archiving and dissemination of macromolecular structure data. PDBe supports diverse research communities in their use of macromolecular structures by enriching the PDB data and by providing advanced tools and services for effective data access, visualization and analysis. This paper details the enrichment of data at PDBe, including mapping of RNA structures to Rfam, and identification of molecules that act as cofactors. PDBe has developed an advanced search facility with ∼100 data categories and sequence searches. New features have been included in the LiteMol viewer at PDBe, with updated visualization of carbohydrates and nucleic acids. Small molecules are now mapped more extensively to external databases and their visual representation has been enhanced. These advances help users to more easily find and interpret macromolecular structure data in order to solve scientific problems.

result.paraphrase: Abstract The Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe), one of the founding members of the Worldwide Protein Data Bank (wwPDB), is actively involved in the deposition, curation, validation, archiving, and distribution of macromolecular structure data. By enriching PDB data and offering advanced tools and services for efficient access, visualization, and analysis, PDBe supports a wide range of research communities in using macromolecular structures. This paper describes PDBe’s data enrichment efforts, including mapping RNA structures to Rfam and identifying molecules that function as cofactors. PDBe has also created an advanced search facility with approximately 100 data categories plus sequence searches. The LiteMol viewer at PDBe now includes new features, with improved visualization of carbohydrates and nucleic acids. Small molecules are mapped more extensively to external databases, and their visual display has been enhanced. Together, these developments make it easier for users to locate and interpret macromolecular structure data for solving scientific problems.
